expected.title: Homological support and the tensor-product formula for arbitrary objects in rigidly-compactly generated tensor-triangulated categories
expected.author: Paul Balmer
expected.difficulty_reason: Standard Day convolution, Gabriel localisation and pure-injective representability do not by themselves identify the maximal localising tensor ideals needed for this support. The author establishes the unique maximal localising tensor ideal extending a given maximal Serre ideal, using the internal-Hom kernel of its pure-injective residue weak ring and injective-hull comparisons across quotients. This nonroutine correspondence supplies the vanishing dichotomy that proves the tensor-product formula for arbitrary noncompact objects.

expected.title: Image of a homological spectrum map as support of the adjoint unit
expected.author: Paul Balmer
expected.difficulty_reason: With the explicit Yoneda/Day, Gabriel-localization, BKS2019 tensor-kernel recovery and adjoint infrastructure allowed, the complete solution still has three research-level structural obligations. It identifies the unique maximal localizing tensor ideal through a pure-injective weak ring; constructs a maximal pulled-back homological prime and lifts the residue injective hull as a direct summand; then forces existence of a prime over a support point using a finitely presented kernel witness and the projection formula. This linked noncompact-support construction and detection argument, rather than the length or publication venue, supports H3. Root adopted the two independent H3 judgments for the unchanged full proof scope; revision-bound review files are required before ready status.

expected.title: For a big tt-category whose compacts are local, reducedness of the fibre of the comparison map over zero is equivalent to a nilpotence alternative for two composable maps of compacts with vanishing tensor product
expected.author: Paul Balmer
expected.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the theorem at source lines 881-893, label Thm:hom-local, printed as Theorem A.1: for a big tt-category whose compact-rigid subcategory is local, the assertion that the fibre of the comparison map from the homological to the triangular spectrum over zero is a single point is equivalent to a nilpotence alternative, namely that whenever two maps f and g of compacts satisfy f tensor g = 0, one of them is tensor-nilpotent on some non-zero compact. The proof at source lines 895-907 constructs the bridge between the two statements rather than observing it: in one direction it builds the Serre tensor-ideal B_0 of finitely presented modules admitting a non-zero compact that kills them, verifies closure under extensions from locality of the compacts, passes to the Gabriel quotient, and proves that a maximal tensor-ideal of the quotient has zero preimage in the compacts exactly when it contains B_0, which uses the embedding of the quotient unit into the dual of a compact tensored with itself; then it shows that both kernels of f and g would have to be contained in the unique maximal tensor-ideal, forcing a monomorphism into a tensor product of flat objects and contradicting f tensor g = 0. The converse direction uses E_B tensor E_C = 0 for distinct homological primes, finite presentability of the unit to factor the units of the pure-injectives through compacts, and the weak-ring property to convert nilpotence into E_B tensor z = 0. Neither implication is a formal consequence of the definitions, and the appendix theorem is the paper's only unconditional characterization of injectivity of the comparison map.

expected.title: The Serre tensor ideal cut out by a homological functor, and the localisation diagram it produces
expected.author: Paul Balmer
expected.difficulty_reason: The lemma works with a big tensor-triangulated category mT satisfying the standing hypothesis and a Serre tensor ideal cC, and claims that the full subcategory cB of objects whose image under hat F lies in cC is a maximal Serre tensor ideal, that a four-square diagram of localisations and adjoints commutes in the four stated ways, and that the pure-injective object EB is a direct summand of U(EC) (statement lines 765-785). The proof applies the homological-functor criterion to the composite H = Q_cC o hat F o yoneda_T, factors it through the localisation at cB, and then compares the two right adjoints of the same functor to obtain R_cB o bar U = hat U o R_cC (proof lines 795-813). The step that carries the content is that comparison of right adjoints: it is what transfers the injective-hull decomposition from the localised category AB to the original category cT, and the author explicitly notes that the decomposition already holds in cT by a cited clause. The argument uses Grothendieck-category theory in the form of a right-adjoint existence statement rather than a computation. H2.

expected.title: Nested localising tensor ideals give isomorphic weak rings of the associated pure-injectives
expected.author: Paul Balmer
expected.difficulty_reason: The proposition is about a proper localising tensor ideal cC containing a localising tensor ideal cB, and claims that the weak rings EB and EC attached to the two ideals are isomorphic in the ambient category in a way compatible with their unit maps (statement lines 505-508). The proof factors the Gabriel quotient into two steps and computes the intermediate object tilde E as the image of EC in the intermediate quotient, then runs an injective-hull argument: the unit is a monomorphism by a cited criterion, the injective hull of the unit in the intermediate category maps into tilde E by a split monomorphism, and exactness of the intermediate localisation together with full faithfulness of its right adjoint forces the complementary summand to vanish (proof lines 511-533). The step that carries the content is that vanishing argument, since it is what converts a split monomorphism into an isomorphism; the descent to the ambient category is then a cited clause. H2.
